objective: Sell and deliver bounded USD 250 bilingual study packs for customer-owned or clearly licensed lectures, using public transcript, book, subtitle, and provenance workflows without implying customer proof or rights to third-party recordings.

executed_media_sample.source: project-created 30-second science short; no customer or third-party lecture media
verified_outputs: 15 timestamped lines aligned across Japanese, English, and Chinese
five transcript-checked concept pointers with exact segment edges
source and rights manifest with the canonical media SHA-256
executed_media_sample.claim_boundary: This is a reproducible project-owned process demonstration, not an automated LKT import, scientific finding, customer result, or proof of rights to unrelated media.

included_scope: one customer-owned or qualifying openly licensed English lecture up to 20 minutes
one target language: Traditional Chinese or Japanese
timestamped English Markdown transcript and SRT with uncertainties marked
an editable bilingual source and A5 pocket study PDF
one customer-selected 30–45 second captioned preview clip
one consolidated pass of up to ten timing, transcription, or terminology corrections
excluded_scope: rights clearance or URL-only platform downloads
additional languages, certified translation, or certified accessibility
custom illustration, dubbing, or generated footage
full-course work, hosting, LMS or social posting, or unlimited revisions
limits: Public availability is not permission to make a commercial derivative. Require customer ownership or an exact license that permits the requested translation and reuse.
The public repositories and Classical Mechanics article demonstrate a workflow and output format, not a paid customer result, lecturer endorsement, translation certification, or sales lift.
Do not request a source file, create a Stripe payment request, or begin delivery until the metadata-only fit check and written scope are accepted.
Mark unresolved recognition, terminology, equation, timing, and translation uncertainties for customer subject review.

funnel.free_value: A searchable project-owned multilingual video with exact timestamp evidence, subtitle exports, and a source manifest, plus a complete Classical Mechanics lesson and public transcript-to-book workflows that a buyer can inspect before enquiring.
funnel.qualified_interest: Use the metadata-only fit check to review source ownership, duration, speaker count, audio, target language, learner, terminology, excerpt rights, and intended distribution.
funnel.commercial_action: After a positive fit review, accept one exact USD 250 scope, receive a reviewed Stripe payment request, and then arrange a private source-file transfer.
funnel.revenue_policy: Count revenue only after confirmed payment; visits, fit-check drafts, emails, likes, queued posts, and source transfers are not sales.

payment.policy: The public price is fixed, but a real Stripe request still requires a qualified buyer, accepted written scope, and reviewed delivery, correction, cancellation, refund, tax, and support terms.

linkedin.content:
A lecture becomes much easier to reuse once every line is tied to time.

I made a small, checkable workflow: correct the source transcript, mark uncertain words, align one target language, export SRT/VTT, and turn the same source into a pocket study PDF. The public proof lets you search Japanese, English, and Chinese and jump to the exact second.

I’m testing the workflow as a fixed USD 250 pack for one rights-cleared English lecture up to 20 minutes. The scope and working proof are here:

practical_guide.content:
A lecture can have accurate words and still make a poor study resource if its transcript, translation, subtitles, and notes each become a separate copy.

A safer workflow is to correct the timed source once, preserve stable segment IDs, derive the subtitle and pocket-book formats from it, then test a translated term by seeking back to the exact second.

I wrote out the full method with a small, working three-language example:
https://blog.lazying.art/html/computer_internet/3792/turn-lecture-into-bilingual-subtitles-study-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=bilingual_lecture_pack_pilot&utm_content=source_first_guide

What changes when every line of a lecture is tied to time? You can search a word and jump straight to the source second.

This short LazyingArt proof uses one project-owned line aligned in Japanese, English, and Chinese. The workflow produces a corrected timestamped transcript, English and target-language SRT files, an editable bilingual source with an A5 pocket PDF, and a source-and-rights manifest.
